meta.title: Hartwell & Okafor | Family law, wills and probate, Islington
meta.description: A small Islington law practice for divorce, children arrangements, wills, lasting powers of attorney and probate. Fixed fees where we can. Free 20 minute first call.

rationale: A local bulletin look suits a small neighbourhood practice: white paper, black ink and one dark red spot colour read as sober and trustworthy, which is what worried clients need. Ruled ledgers, numbered labels and narrow text columns let us explain services, costs and process plainly. The editorial hero puts the practical facts (free call, fixed fees, address) beside the headline, and the question-and-answer process answers the fear of cost directly.

props.label: What we do
props.title: Three areas of law, handled by the same small team
props.intro: You deal with a partner from the first call to the last letter. Where the work is predictable we quote a fixed fee before we start.

items.name: Divorce and separation
items.description: Ending a marriage or civil partnership, dividing money and property, and agreeing the practical steps calmly and in the right order.

items.name: Arrangements for children
items.description: Where children will live, how time is shared, and how to put that in writing so everyone knows where they stand.

items.name: Wills
items.description: Wills for individuals and couples, written clearly so your wishes are followed and your family is not left guessing.

items.name: Lasting powers of attorney

items.name: Probate

props.note: Ask on the free call whether your matter can be done for a fixed fee. We will give you the figure in writing before any work begins.

props.label: How it works
props.title: What you are probably wondering, and what we do about it

pairs.ask: I do not even know where to begin.
pairs.answer: Book the free 20 minute call. You tell us what has happened, we tell you your options in plain words. There is nothing to prepare and no obligation to go further.

pairs.ask: What is this going to cost me?
pairs.answer: Where we can, we quote a fixed fee. Where we cannot, we explain why, give you an estimate, and tell you before costs move beyond it.

pairs.ask: Will I have to deal with a stranger each time?
pairs.answer: No. One of the two partners looks after your matter, helped by our paralegal. You will always know who has your file.

pairs.ask: What happens after we decide to go ahead?
pairs.answer: We confirm the fee and the plan in a short letter, then take it step by step. After each stage we tell you what is done and what comes next.

props.label: About us
props.title: A small practice, on purpose
paragraphs: Hartwell & Okafor is two partners, Clare Hartwell and Tunde Okafor, and a paralegal. We work from Islington, and most of the people we help live nearby.

Most people come to us at a difficult time: a marriage ending, a parent who has died, a will that has been put off for years. They are often worried about what it will cost and what they will be asked to do.
So we keep things plain. We explain the law without jargon, we say what will happen next, and we agree the fee early. You should never have to chase us to find out where your matter stands.
We are a small team and we like it that way. It means the person who answers the phone knows your file.
props.pullQuote: You should never have to chase us to find out where your matter stands.

quotes.text: I was dreading the first call. Twenty minutes later I knew what the next three steps were and what they would cost.
They dealt with my mother's probate with patience, and I always knew who to ring.
Our wills and powers of attorney were done in two meetings at the price we were quoted.

items.q: Is the first call really free?
items.a: Yes. It lasts 20 minutes, it is free, and you are under no obligation to instruct us afterwards.
Where we can. Many wills, powers of attorney and straightforward matters have a fixed fee we agree with you in advance. For work that is harder to predict, we explain why and give an estimate.

items.q: What should I bring to the first call?
items.a: Nothing is required. If you have a few key documents to hand, such as a marriage certificate or an existing will, it can help, but we can start without them.

items.q: Do I have to go to court?
items.a: Not always. Many family matters are settled by agreement. We will tell you honestly if court looks likely and what that would involve.

items.q: Can you help if I do not live in Islington?
items.a: Yes. Many conversations can happen by phone or video, and we will tell you when a meeting in person would help.
